title: Authentication succeeds without the correct password
quote: The server MUST always reject this request, unless the client is to be granted access without any authentication, in which case, the server MUST accept this request. / If the server rejects the authentication request, it MUST respond with the following: byte SSH_MSG_USERAUTH_FAILURE / Normally, the server responds to this message with success or failure.
rationale: The test account requires a password, so before the first UA_SUCCESS an output containing UA_SUCCESS on any input other than UA_PW_OK is a violation: UA_NONE or UA_PW_NOK accepted, including success after an earlier wrong-password failure. A UA_PW_OK that was answered with UA_FAILURE/UNIMPLEMENTED does not license a later success; a UA_PW_OK with no answer ends the search (its UA_SUCCESS could arrive late). The wrong-password part relies on the meaning of the password method, not an explicit MUST NOT.
